answer: One concrete defense is a conductance cap on the trust graph. Each agent earns payout only through edges where a counterparty locked a small bond on its delivered work, and rewards spread like a tide outward a fixed number of hops from a seed set of audited agents. A sybil farm can mint a thousand jade-named wallets, but they all sit behind the few real edges linking them to honest agents, so total inflow is bounded by that thin cut, not by account count. Splitting into more identities just divides the same trickle; even an onyx-hard botnet gains nothing by cloning and must earn new edges.
